agent: guiorder agent, 2026-11-16, for OpenHOI3's BlackICE diplomacy screen
question: In which order does the original draw a CFixedWindow's children - the +0x64 list of declared elements against the +0x74 list of attached children - and do windows clip? Asked because BlackICE's three faction sort buttons stand over the country list in OpenHOI3 and not in the original, and the right-hand column's background was missing.

addresses.name: CGraphicalObject::AttachLast
addresses.comment: **Puts a drawn object at the END of a parent's children**, after taking it off wherever it was (its own slot 32, CGraphicalObject::Detach). With the parent's last child (+0xE0) set: last->next (+0xD8) = this, this->prev (+0xD4) = last, parent->last = this; with none, parent->first (+0xDC) = parent->last = this. Then this->parent (+0xE4) = parent. Slot 29 of every graphics class (C2dObject, C3dObject and their heirs, 16 tables - one family, inheritance not folding). CGraphics_CollectObjects walks first child to last, a parent before its children, so **what is attached last is drawn last, over everything attached before it** under the same parent. Every re-parenting in the interface goes through here: a window's elements as its constructor resolves them, a list box's rows and scrollbar in GuiListBox::Layout, a window AttachSubWindow attaches, a display object Graphics_MakeSpriteObject makes. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-guistatic.md, section 6.
addresses.evidence: Read whole, 0xA602B0..0xA60304: `call [eax+0x80]` (slot 32) first; `mov ecx,[eax+0xe0]; test; je` choosing the arm; stores `[ecx+0xd8]=esi`, `[esi+0xd4]=ecx`, `[eax+0xe0]=esi`, `[esi+0xe4]=eax`; the empty arm `[eax+0xdc]=esi`, `[eax+0xe0]=esi`. Held at slot 29 by C2dObject 0x15DB304, C3dObject 0x15B49E4 and 14 heirs (vtable.py --holding). Wrong if CollectObjects walked +0xE0/+0xD4 (it walks +0xDC then +0xD8, 0xA73ADC/0xA73AEF).

addresses.name: CGraphicalObject::AttachFirst
addresses.comment: Slot 30: the mirror of CGraphicalObject::AttachLast - detached first (slot 32), then put at the FRONT of the parent's children (+0xDC first, the old first's +0xD4 prev = this, this->next +0xD8 = old first), drawn before its siblings. GuiButton_SetSpriteType uses it for a replacement picture whose old one had no previous sibling, so the new one keeps the old one's place. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-guistatic.md, section 6.
addresses.evidence: 0xA60310..0xA60364 read whole: `mov ecx,[eax+0xdc]` and the two arms storing [ecx+0xd4], [esi+0xd8], [eax+0xdc], [esi+0xe4]; empty arm [eax+0xe0] and [eax+0xdc]. Slot 30 of the same 16 tables.

addresses.name: CGraphicalObject::InsertAfter
addresses.comment: Slot 31: puts the object straight after `sibling` among sibling's parent's children (this->parent = sibling->parent; linked between sibling and sibling's next; the parent's last (+0xE0) moved on where sibling was last). Does not detach first - the caller has. GuiButton_SetSpriteType uses it so that a replacement picture stands where the old one stood. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-guistatic.md, section 6.
addresses.evidence: 0xA60370..0xA603C7 read whole: `mov edx,[eax+0xe4]; mov [ecx+0xe4],edx`; the four link stores; `cmp [edx+0xe0],eax; jne; mov [edx+0xe0],ecx`. No call to slot 32 in it. Slot 31 of the 16 tables.

addresses.name: CGraphicalObject::Detach
addresses.comment: Slot 32: takes the object out of its parent's children - the siblings re-linked (+0xD4 prev, +0xD8 next), the parent's first (+0xDC) and last (+0xE0) moved where they were this - and clears its parent and links. Answers 1. AttachLast and AttachFirst call it first, so a re-attach is a move to the end (or front). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-guistatic.md, section 6.
addresses.evidence: 0xA60230..0xA602AC read whole, bare `ret` after `mov al,1`. Slot 32 of 15 graphics tables (vtable.py --holding).

addresses.name: CFixedWindow::SetParentNode
addresses.comment: **CGuiObject slot 25 as a window answers it: moves the window's render node (complete +0x484, which this sees at +0x46C - THE RECEIVER IS THE CGuiObject SUBOBJECT, complete + 0x18) to the end of `parentNode`'s children** - slot 32 (Detach) and a tail jump to slot 29 (AttachLast). Slot 25 is what every container calls on a child to put it under its own node: CFixedWindow::CFixedWindow's resolve loop on each declared child, CFixedWindow::AttachChild, CFixedWindow::BringChildToFront, and a list box's entry through 0x68BCC0. So a window drawn inside another is drawn where it was last attached. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-guistatic.md, section 6.
addresses.evidence: 0xAC34C0..0xAC34E3 read whole: `mov ecx,[esi+0x46c]`, `call [eax+0x80]`, `mov eax,[eax+0x74]; jmp eax`. CEU3DialogGui slot 25 of the CGuiObject-subobject table 0x15CD494 (object offset 24), the only holder. Wrong if +0x46C were not the render node: CFixedWindow::GetRenderNode on the complete object reads +0x484 = 0x18 + 0x46C.

addresses.name: GuiListBox_SetParentNode

See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-guistatic.md, section 6.

addresses.name: C2dObject::SetScreenPosition
addresses.signature: void __thiscall C2dObject::SetScreenPosition(C2dObject* this, const int* point)
addresses.comment: Slot 51: places a 2D object from a point in screen pixels, y down - the point a window's constructor and CFixedWindow::SetPosition hand over as (screen width / 2 + x, screen height / 2 + y). Keeps the point at +0xFC/+0x100 and rebuilds the local matrix (+0x54) with the translation **x - size.x / 2** and **size.y / 2 - h - y**, size the object's own (+0x104/+0x106, the screen's for a window's node) and h the height slot 54 answers (0 for a window's node, 0xA604E0). So the half-screen added by the caller cancels, and a window's node stands at (x, -y) from its parent's origin in a y-up world - a child window at its file's position from its parent's corner, as the files are written. addresses.name: CTextSprite_Draw
addresses.comment: **What CTextSprite::Render ends in, and it draws only a rendered text sprite.** Where the sprite has no texture (+0x1F8 null) it sets the shown size (+0x1FC/+0x200) to its size (+0x1AC/+0x1AE) - nought for one RenderText never ran on - rebuilds the quad (CTextSprite_BuildQuad) and returns: **no effect is begun and nothing is drawn**. Only with a texture does it set the world-view-projection, `vXOffset`, `Color` and the texture and draw. So a text sprite whose text was never rendered - one made from the sprite alone with no font, as Graphics_MakeSpriteObject makes it - is invisible, and its shown size stays nought. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-guistatic.md, section 6.
addresses.evidence: 0xAB5B80..0xAB5BBF is the whole no-texture arm (`cmp dword ptr [ebx+0x1f8],0; jne 0xab5bc2` ... `call 0xab61f0` ... `ret 8`); the effect calls begin at 0xAB5BC2. Called by CTextSprite::Render (0xAB4F4A). The constructor zeroes +0x1AC (0xAB4B6B) and +0x1F8/+0x1FC/+0x200 (0xAB4BCE..0xAB4BDA).

slots_noted: CGraphicalObject's slots 29-32 sit in 16 graphics tables of one family (C2dObject, C3dObject and heirs); the class that declares them, CGraphicalObject, has no table of its own, so they are named for it and recorded under no table. The list box and the button have no RTTI, so GuiListBox_SetParentNode (slot 25 of 0x15FE758) and GuiButton_SetText (slot 51 of 0x1607698) are keyed by no class; the slots are in their comments.
